data.name: Druvithansh
data.long_meaning:
Druvithansh is derived from the words ‘Druv’ meaning sun, star and ‘Ithansh’ meaning Lord of Gods, Indra.
It is believed that this name was given to the sage Druvasena, the father of the great hero Bhagiratha who brought Lord Shiva down to the earth to absolve the sins of his ancestors.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radiates the power of the Sun and is blessed by the Lord of Gods.

in_sanskrit.name: द्रुविथान्श
in_sanskrit.meaning: Dharma (law, moral order) + Vitha (wisdom) + Ansh (sign, symbol, essence)
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: One who embodies the essence of dharma (law, moral order) and possesses great wisdom.

in_hindi.name: द्रुविथान्श
in_hindi.long_meaning:
द्रुवि (द्रव्य, धर्म) + थान्श (विद्या, विज्ञान + अन्न,न, अन्नकर्ता) = द्रुविथान्श
One who possesses wisdom and knowledge (Vitha) and embodies the essence of Dharma (law, moral order, dharma) and is a giver of food and nourishment (Ansh, Annayan, Annakarta).

in_tamil.name: திருவிதாஞ்சம்
in_tamil.meaning: திரு (Dharma, moral law) + விதா (Vitha, wisdom) + ஞ்சம் (Ansh, essence)
in_tamil.long_meaning: One who embodies the essence of moral law (Dharma) and possesses great wisdom (Vitha).

in_telugu.name: ద్రువిథాన్శ
in_telugu.long_meaning: One who possesses wisdom and knowledge (Vidhyayudhudhesham, Vijjadeesham) and embodies the essence of Dharma (धर्म) and is a giver of food and nourishment (Anna-dhesham, Annadhesham).

data.cultural_impact: The name Druvithansh carries a rich and profound cultural heritage that represents the divine connection between eternal celestial bodies and Hindu deities. It is a reminder of the important role that our spiritual leaders, symbolized by the sage Druvasena, play in ensuring the purification of our ancestral lineage and connection to the divine realm.
data.spiritual_significance: Furthermore, the name Druvithansh holds immense spiritual significance as it embody the Hindu values of dharma, artha, kama, and moksha. Druva, the celestial entity, represents dharma, the eternal law of the universe, while Indra, the Lord of Gods, represents spiritual power and wisdom. Together, this name signifies the importance of upholding spiritual truths, seeking spiritual growth, and ultimately, attaining spiritual liberation.

historical_references.reference: Druvida Raja, also known as Druvithan, was a king of the Satavahana dynasty in the 1st century BC. He is known for his inscriptions found at Amaravati Stupa in Andhra Pradesh, which provide important historical and epigraphic information about the kingdom during the Satavahana period.

Druvithan is also mentioned in the Jataka tales, a collection of Buddhist stories, as a sage who was a former king. According to the tales, Druvithan renounced his throne to become a monk and attain enlightenment. The tales provide a legend about the origins of the Druvida Raja of the Satavahana period.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, possibly before the Satavahana period
